title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Mathematics · Chapter 2 Polynomials (NCERT reprint 2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions modelled on question types that have repeated in CBSE board papers 2023-2026 and the Sample Question Papers 2024-25 to 2026-27. They are practice for readiness, not predictions of what will appear in any exam.
instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (negative allowed). No calculator.

patterns.P2: Form a polynomial from zeroes / sum and product
patterns.P3: Value of an α, β expression
patterns.P4: Find k from a condition on the zeroes

S1.name: Degree, value p(k) and zeroes
S1.tip: Degree = highest power. k is a zero when p(k) = 0: substitute carefully with brackets for negatives. Zero of ax + b is −b/a.

S2.name: Zeroes on a graph (geometric meaning)
S2.tip: Zeroes are where the graph meets the x-axis. A touching point counts once; the y-axis crossing never counts. Degree n → at most n zeroes.

S3.name: Sum and product of zeroes
S3.tip: Sum = −b/a, product = c/a. Put the polynomial in standard form ax² + bx + c before reading a, b, c.

S4.name: Find the zeroes and verify
S4.tip: Rearrange, split the middle term, set each factor to 0, then verify sum and product against −b/a and c/a.

S5.name: Form a quadratic polynomial
S5.tip: Use k[x² − (sum)x + product] and choose k to clear fractions. From zeroes: add and multiply them first. Infinitely many polynomials share two zeroes.

S6.name: Expressions in α and β
S6.tip: Rewrite every expression with α + β and αβ: α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ, (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ, 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/αβ.
S6.ncert: Past-paper type built on NCERT §2.3 (no direct NCERT exercise)

S7.name: Find k from a condition on the zeroes
S7.tip: Translate the condition: reciprocal → c = a; given zero r → p(r) = 0; sum = product → −b/a = c/a; one zero m times the other → α and mα.

S8.name: Case study: height polynomial
S8.tip: For h(t) = bt − at², the zeroes are the start and landing times; the highest point is midway between them.
S8.ncert: Case-study type (2023, 2024 papers); revise NCERT §2.2 graphs

questions.question: What is the degree of the polynomial 7x − 4x³ + 2?
questions.explanation: The highest power of x is 3.

questions.question: Which of these is a quadratic polynomial?
questions.explanation: Degree 2 with whole-number powers only. 1/x and √x are not polynomials.

questions.question: If p(x) = x² − 4x + 1, find p(3).
questions.remediation: Video part 1: put 3 in place of x.

questions.question: Which number is a zero of x² + x − 6?
questions.explanation: x² + x − 6 = (x + 3)(x − 2), so the zeroes are 2 and −3. Check: p(2) = 4 + 2 − 6 = 0.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: k is a zero when p(k) = 0.

questions.question: The zero of the linear polynomial 3x + 7 is:

questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the degree of a non-zero constant does not explain why the zero polynomial has no degree.
questions.assertion: The degree of the zero polynomial is not defined.
questions.reason: The degree of a non-zero constant polynomial is 0.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.explanation: Zeroes make y = p(x) = 0, i.e. points on the x-axis.

questions.question: At most how many zeroes can a cubic polynomial have?
questions.explanation: Degree n → at most n zeroes.

questions.question: The graph of y = p(x) crosses the x-axis at x = −3 and x = 1, touches it at x = 4, and crosses the y-axis at y = 5. It meets the x-axis nowhere else. How many zeroes does p(x) have?
questions.explanation: −3, 1 and 4 (a touch counts). The y-axis crossing is not a zero.

questions.question: The graph of y = ax² + bx + c opens downwards. Then:
questions.explanation: A parabola opens down when a is negative.

questions.question: The graph of a quadratic polynomial passes through (−4, 0), (0, −8), (2, 0) and (3, 7). Its zeroes are:
questions.explanation: Zeroes are where y = 0: x = −4 and x = 2. (The polynomial is x² + 2x − 8.)

questions.question: The graph of y = x² + 2x + 3 meets the x-axis at:
questions.explanation: x² + 2x + 3 = (x + 1)² + 2 is always at least 2, so it never equals 0: no zeroes.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: a quadratic can have 0 zeroes.

questions.question: A ball's height after t seconds is h(t) = 20t − 5t² metres. After how many seconds does it come back to the ground?
questions.explanation: 5t(4 − t) = 0 → t = 0 or 4; it lands at t = 4.

questions.question: For the same ball, h(t) = 20t − 5t² metres, what is the greatest height (in metres)?
questions.explanation: The top is midway between the zeroes 0 and 4, at t = 2: h = 40 − 20 = 20 m.
